newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish referendum adopts constitution-exit poll.
newsitem.headline: Polish referendum adopts constitution-exit poll.

text.p: Poles voted in a referendum on Sunday to adopt a new constitution which was backed by the ruling ex-communists and strongly opposed by the right-leaning opposition, the first exit poll suggested.

A poll by the Pracownia Badan Spolecznych (PBS) showed that 56.8 percent had voted for the new constitution and 43.2 were against in a turnout of 39.8 percent of Poland's 28 million voters, public television reported.

The polls was based on questions posed to voters at 360 stations around the country. A PBS official said previous such polls after other national votes had never differed by more than one percent from the official results. The final result will be published late on Monday or on Tuesday.

The constitution, designed to enshrine Poland's democratic transformation since the 1989 fall of communism, was drafted by the ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and its Peasant allies with two opposition parties in parliament.

The Solidarity trade union and its rightist allies grouped in an alliance which aims to supplant the ex-communists in elections due in September had urged voters to reject it, saying it failed to reflect Poland's Christian traditions and safeguard national sovereignty.
President Aleksander Kwasniewski, an ex-communist, welcomed the outcome but Solidarity alliance representatives said they would seek to change elements of the constitution if they won the elections.
